paragraphs: Kent runs one of the larger school estates in England — 459 primary and 100 secondary schools, spread across market towns, villages and denser urban centres.
The largest concentrations sit around Maidstone, Canterbury, Ashford, which together account for a meaningful share of the council's pupil places.
Selective schools are part of the mix in Kent — for those, passing the admissions test comes first and catchment distance only applies as a tiebreaker.
The catchment boundary for any given school is defined in the council's annual admissions booklet — we link to that search for every Kent school below.
Lancashire runs one of the larger school estates in England — 480 primary and 80 secondary schools, spread across market towns, villages and denser urban centres.
Expect the tightest competition in and around Preston and Burnley, where popular primaries are regularly oversubscribed and last-distance-offered figures can shrink to a few hundred metres.

Around 48% of schools in Lancashire have a religious character — Church of England, Catholic, or other faith — which means faith criteria sit alongside catchment distance in those schools' oversubscription tiebreakers.
For the exact catchment map and the previous year's last-distance-offered figure, always check Lancashire's current admissions policy before assuming your postcode is inside a school's boundary.
